text:
lena: Heads up — we're seeing a burst of pod evictions on the gpu nodepool. Kubelet is marking nodes as network-unavailable and evicting pods. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: Yup, saw alerts. Evictions started ~10m ago. Net metrics show higher east-west latency and some packet drops between rack switches.

ashley: Quick check — are the affected nodes on different NIC firmware? Yesterday's kernel/driver roll hit a subset of hosts. RDMA nodes seem untouched.

lena: Good call. Affected nodes are in rg-us-east-2b and are non-RDMA. I pulled a kubelet log snippet from one node:

ashley: ```
May 12 15:11:02 kubelet[1234]: W0512 15:11:02.123456   1234 network.go:245] Network probe failed: ping gateway failed: packet loss=30%
May 12 15:11:02 kubelet[1234]: I0512 15:11:02.123789   1234 kubelet_node_status.go:401] Setting node condition NetworkUnavailable=true
May 12 15:11:03 eviction-manager[1234]: Evicting 12 pods for node condition
```

mike: That packet loss looks like fragmentation. I ran tcpdump and saw ICMP fragmentation when MTU differs end-to-end. Edge of our spine has 9000 but some leaf links negotiated 1500 after a transceiver flapped.

infra-bot: alert: ops-alerts: 6 nodes reported kubelet.network_unavailable within 15m window. See: https://console.internal/alerts/5421

ryan: Did we recently enable VXLAN offload on that cluster? VXLAN + jumbo can cause mismatch if offload settings differ between kernel and firmware.

ashley: We did enable GENEVE offload last week as part of perf tests on a canary subset. Can confirm the nodes with evictions are in the canary label set.

lena: Ok that narrows it. So hypothesis: new overlay offload + partial firmware/kernel roll -> MTU/fragmentation -> kubelet network probe pings fail -> kubelet sets NetworkUnavailable -> eviction-controller removes pods (including GPU workloads).

mike: Short-term mitigation: increase kubelet net-probe retries/timeouts or disable the network probe on gpu nodegroup so we don't evict expensive pods while we patch. We should be careful with global kubelet flags though.

ashley: Command to inspect current kubelet config on a node:
```
kubectl get node ip-10-0-2-17 -o yaml | yq ".status.conditions[] | select(.type==\"NetworkUnavailable\")"
cat /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml | grep -i network
```

ryan: Proposal: 1) Patch the overlay offload config rollback on affected canary ASG, 2) bump kubelet probe timeout to 10s and retries to 5 on that nodepool via MachineDeployment override, 3) roll the canary hosts with firmware fix.

lena: Agreed. Also let's exempt gpu-critical taints from eviction while we remediate (temporary).

mike: I'll open a fast PR for a kubelet KubeletConfiguration patch and target the gpu nodegroup. Will also add a short-lived autoscaler rule to avoid draining during the fix.

ashley: I'll rollback the offload change on the canary ASG and start a firmware verification job.

infra-bot: deployment-bot: kubelet-config-pr created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/2123 (target: gpu-nodegroup)

ops-alerts: Note: keeping this channel updated. Scheduled maintenance window in 30m for the canary rollback.

lena: Thanks — if rolling fixes the issue we'll adopt the corrected offload settings cluster-wide after QA. If not, we'll revert the feature and re-evaluate RDMA path differences. :thumbsup:

ashley: I'll post postmortem if this ends up causing more than 30m impact.

mike: Adding a small watch script to monitor kubelet NetworkUnavailable transitions and immediately notify on the Slack #eng-infra thread.

lena: Good. Keep updates here and paste any additional logs.
